user.title: User Sessions
user.description: Track every user's sign-ins and long-lived tokens, failed sign-in attempts, and sign users out. Options can be changed afterwards with Configure.

abort.already_configured: User Sessions is already set up.

init.title: User Sessions options
init.description: Which networks and IPs count as yours, how failed sign-ins are captured, and how long cleared entries are kept.

networks.name: Known networks & IPs
networks.description: One entry per line: an address, then an optional label (e.g. `203.0.113.0/24 Work office`). Remove an entry with its ×; type to add a new one.

data_description.known_networks: Address ranges (CIDR) that count as yours: sign-ins from them are 'known' and never flagged. Pre-filled with your home LAN and Tailscale.
data_description.known_ips: Single IPs that count as yours. Pre-filled with every outside IP that has signed in successfully, plus IPs you trusted from an alert. Removing one forgets it.
data_description.known_radius_km: A public IP that geolocates within this distance of your home zone counts as a known location.

data.lookup_mac: Look up the device (MAC address) for attempts from your local network
data.notify_on_ban: Notify me what to block when Home Assistant bans an IP
data.dismiss_ha_notification: Also dismiss HA's 'Login attempt failed' notification when cleared

data_description.track_failed: Record every wrong password and every request with a bad token (from Home Assistant's own log), with IP, location, browser and device.
data_description.geo_provider: Looks up only public IPs, never LAN or Tailscale ones. Results are cached for 7 days.
data_description.lookup_mac: Only possible on the same network segment as Home Assistant; internet and Tailscale attempts never reveal a MAC. Uses the system's ARP table and any router integration's device trackers. Nothing is blocked.
data_description.notify_on_ban: Needs IP banning turned on (Settings → System → Network → HTTP server). Shows the IP, device and MAC with steps to block it on your own router or firewall, and fires a user_sessions_ip_banned event for your own automations.
data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between checks for new sign-ins and long-lived tokens.

data.auto_archive_days: Auto-move uncleared failed sign-ins to history after

data_description.history_retention_days: Cleared entries older than this are deleted automatically.
data_description.history_max_entries: Oldest entries are deleted once history passes this size.
data_description.auto_archive_days: 0 = never; uncleared entries stay until you clear them.

dashboard.name: Dashboard card (optional)
dashboard.description: A small, theme-aware card that ships with this integration. Add it from the card picker as **User Sessions**, or in YAML as `type: custom:user-sessions-card` with `view: failed`, `sessions` or `summary`.

data_description.enable_card: Serves the card from the integration and loads it into your dashboards: no HACS frontend download or manual resource needed. Turning it off unloads it; cards already on a dashboard then show as missing.

error.invalid_network: Not a valid network: {bad}. Use CIDR like 192.168.1.0/24, optionally followed by a label.
error.invalid_ip: Not a valid IP: {bad}. Use an address like 203.0.113.7, optionally followed by a label.

sign_out_user.name: Sign out user
sign_out_user.description: Remove every sign-in of one user.

user_id.name: User ID
user_id.description: The user's ID (or use user name).

include_long_lived.name: Include long-lived tokens
include_long_lived.description: Also revoke the user's long-lived access tokens.

sign_out_session.name: Sign out session
sign_out_session.description: Revoke one sign-in or one long-lived token.

session_id.name: Session ID
session_id.description: session_id from a user sensor's attributes.

clear_failed_sign_ins.name: Clear failed sign-ins
clear_failed_sign_ins.description: Move failed sign-ins to history. With no fields, clears all of them.

entry_id.name: Entry ID
entry_id.description: Clear one entry (id from the Failed sign-ins sensor).

ip.name: IP address
ip.description: Clear the entry for this IP.

clear_history.name: Clear failed sign-in history
clear_history.description: Delete history entries. With no fields, deletes all of them.

older_than_days.name: Older than
older_than_days.description: Only delete entries cleared more than this many days ago.

trust_ip.name: Trust IP
trust_ip.description: Mark an IP (and the devices seen from it) as yours, so it counts as known.

forget_ip.name: Forget IP
forget_ip.description: Remove an IP from the known/trusted list.
